description: The plot illustrates how accuracy metrics vary as a function of “Initial Confidence,” showing three accuracy-related series with error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” on a linear scale, with tick labels running from 0.81 to 0.99 (shown at discrete values including 0.81, 0.82, then 0.84 through 0.99 in steps of 0.01). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” on a linear scale, spanning 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The blue series (“Final Accuracy”) is a solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it starts at about 1.00 at initial confidence 0.81, stays around the high 0.8s to high 0.9s across the axis (e.g., ~0.90 at 0.82, ~0.94 at 0.84, ~0.97 at 0.90), dips to about ~0.86 at 0.95, and ends near ~0.98 at 0.99. The orange series (“Δ Accuracy”) is a dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it begins around ~0.46 at 0.81, declines to ~0.31 at 0.84, drops to about ~0.15 at 0.86, rises to roughly ~0.37 at 0.88, returns to ~0.15 at 0.89, fluctuates in the ~0.14–0.29 range from 0.90 to 0.97 (e.g., ~0.23 at 0.90, ~0.29 at 0.93, ~0.14 at 0.95), and finishes near ~0.04 at 0.99. The green series (“Initial Accuracy”) is a dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it starts around ~0.54 at 0.81, is ~0.52 at 0.82, rises to ~0.63 at 0.84, reaches about ~0.75 at 0.86, dips to ~0.58 at 0.88, returns to ~0.75 at 0.89, varies through the mid-0.6s to mid-0.7s from 0.90 to 0.97 (e.g., ~0.74 at 0.90, ~0.65 at 0.91, ~0.76 at 0.96), then increases to ~0.82 at 0.98 and ends around ~0.93 at 0.99.
